title: Automate meeting notes into your CRM
description: A system that turns your call notes into a CRM-ready update you review before anything writes back.

api.title: API (Application Programming Interface)
api.content: A way for two programs to talk to each other. When a tool says 'connect via API,' it means software can send requests and get data back automatically — no manual copy-paste needed.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

granola.title: Granola
granola.content: An AI meeting notes app that listens to your calls and produces structured summaries, action items, and transcripts. Works in the background during Zoom, Google Meet, and in-person meetings. Useful as a source of raw material for AI workflows — feed transcripts into Claude for follow-ups or CRM updates.

hubspot.title: HubSpot
hubspot.content: A CRM and marketing platform used by sales, marketing, and customer success teams. Common target for AI automations — students connect it to draft outreach, enrich contacts, or sync data with other tools.

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.content: A multi-step process Claude runs to accomplish a goal — for example: read emails → filter by topic → summarize → post to Slack. Workflows can be run manually or on a schedule.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

children.text: Raw AI summaries written straight to CRM fields create noisy records, so [Anthropic's Claude Academy](https://academy.claude.com/use-cases/log-sales-calls-to-your-crm) documents this pattern by name, matching each meeting to its CRM contact and drafting an activity log a person has to approve first.
CRM entry eats a big slice of a rep's week. The biggest failure point in these [workflows](#tooltip-workflow) is bad sync, so the review step belongs in the design from the start.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) right after a call, a saved skill, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) triggered when a transcript lands. Every version holds its proposed updates for your review before anything reaches the CRM.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming your CRM, your notes format, the fields you update after a call, and how much review you want before anything syncs.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns my call notes into clean CRM updates. Ask me questions, one at a time, about which CRM I use, what my notes typically look like, which fields I update after a call, how much review I want first, and what a bad CRM entry looks like. When you have what you need, write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: naming what a bad CRM entry looks like before you build anything gives the system a rule to check itself against, instead of a standard only you can see.

items: Whether transcripts come from a call tool, a notetaker, or handwritten notes.
Who owns the mapping between your notes and specific CRM fields.
Which fields are safe to auto-populate and which need a human eye every time.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your CRM (Salesforce and [HubSpot](#tooltip-hubspot) publish official connectors and [API](#tooltip-api) docs), call intelligence tools like Gong, Fathom, or [Granola](#tooltip-granola), and your calendar to match meetings to contacts. The paste-in version needs none.

**Create.** Start building the system your scope document describes, and test it on a real call, one you already know well enough to check the output. The prompt below is an example of the core task. Your scope document will give you a version shaped to your setup.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn my notes from a call with [account] into a CRM-ready update, held for review.

Context: [Paste your call transcript or notes.] CRM is [Salesforce/HubSpot]. Fields I update after a call are [stage, next steps, notes].

Rules:
- Never write to the CRM directly.
- Output a summary, proposed field changes (old value, new value), and action items with owners.
- Flag anything you're inferring rather than reading directly from the notes.
- Never invent a commitment that isn't in the notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: separating proposed changes from a direct write keeps a wrong guess a one-line edit instead of a corrupted CRM record.

children.text: **Review.** Check the draft against your scope. Field changes shown as old and new, action items with owners, nothing invented?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what went wrong and fold the correction into the rules.

items: Draft a customer-facing recap alongside the CRM update.
Flag any stakeholder on the call who isn't in the CRM yet.
Build a manager's weekly rollup across the team's calls.
Extend the same system to [Slack](#tooltip-slack) or email threads.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat draft the rubric and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each CRM update draft, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, call reviewed, fields changed, corrections I made, and whether I approved it as-is. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the guesswork, and the log columns turn a week of runs into a pattern you can see.

children.text: **Log** every run against the rubric. Note the date, which checks passed or failed, and what changed. After a couple weeks it shows which fields the AI reliably gets right and which ones need a correction almost every time. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes a few weeks straight, package the prompt and your corrected rules into a reusable AI skill, so every run starts from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s built-in skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
One durable failure mode. Skipping review is how CRMs fill with confident, wrong data, so keep the review step built into the system instead of counting on remembering to check.
